dedupe_keys.name: hospital wide discrete event simulation decision support tool planning services and a virtual ward 2023 to 2027

description: This case study presents a user-friendly decision support tool that lets hospital managers and clinicians test the effect of new services and interventions across all hospital operations. The author, at the University of Hertfordshire, built the tool on a discrete event simulation model that covers specialties and the links between hospital services, driven by a dataset of 360 input parameters and statistical distributions, and published it in an open-access journal article. Scenarios for 2023 to 2027 produce activity levels, bed and clinic requirements, operating theatre utilisation and financial implications. Coverage is one hospital; the article does not name its location in the abstract. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the tool and parameter set are not published. Caveats: results depend on the hospital's own parameters, and the tool's usability claims come from the author. The study found that implementing a virtual ward reduced patient backlogs and cut the strain on resources from 113 percent to 80 percent of capacity. Simulation uses: an example of whole-hospital discrete event simulation for capacity planning and service redesign. Related records: the Queensland ward-level simulation (case_study-queensland-hospitals-ward-level-des-access-block) and the British Columbia heatwave simulation (case_study-british-columbia-2021-heatwave-acute-care-des) apply discrete event simulation to hospital capacity.
